On the same cached late-May activity snapshot, auto-dreamer-ckpt-bridge-public and dreamer_sciworld_v2_step60 are 'published' 18 and 17 days earlier, respectively, placing those publication events in early May before Auto-Dreamer v1. Their current cards/file-tree access still do not bind exact evaluated checkpoint bytes to the paper run.

Auto-Dreamer's current public ScienceWorld corpus exposes 30 native task names, 11 functional groups and 6 broad domains, while visible selection artifacts use 11-bank/9type/9cat naming and the paper online evaluation says seven sampled task types over 660 frozen episodes. These populations/taxonomies must remain distinct until row-level deterministic derivation binds them.

The paper's fixed-bank regime is a comparatively strong controlled consolidation intervention: identical pre-built B0 from the same fixed writer, one consolidation, frozen task-agent evaluation; ScienceWorld Auto-Dreamer reports 44.3% SR / 539 tokens versus strongest baseline Mem0 42.0% / 1,609. The find-entity case study further matches task agent, writer, retriever, prompt and task order while ending at near-identical bank footprint (795 vs 816 tokens) and reports 58/80 vs 21/80 success. Without serialized B0/B*, row outcomes, run/checkpoint identity and verifier binding, these remain paper-level evidence rather than scheduled-Chat static replay proof.
